tweet.text:
One prompt spawned 34 sub-agents. The bill came back 15x normal.

I watched an orchestrator fan out with no cap, no budget, no merge plan.
Each child pulled full context, then spawned its own helpers.

What the trace showed the next morning:
- Input tokens up 15x vs a single-agent run on the same task
- 31 of 34 agents returned overlapping research, 3 found nothing new
- Merge step choked on 41k tokens of duplicated findings
- Wall-clock time tripled while answers stayed flat

Fan-out without a task budget is not parallelism. It is a fork bomb with an invoice.

At 11:30 AM: the orchestrator contract that caps fan-out and merges clean.

Would you cap prod fan-out at 3 scoped agents, or let the orchestrator spawn freely?
